newsitem.title: GREECE: Murder charges in Greece over missing immigrants.
newsitem.headline: Murder charges in Greece over missing immigrants.

text.p: Three people have been charged with murder in connection with allegations that some 280 illegal immigrants from India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka were drowned in transit in the Malta-Sicily channel on Christmas Day, Greek court officials said on Thursday.
Prosecutor Yannis Provatas, in Nafplion on the Peloponnese coast, charged another eight people on Wednesday with complicity in the case and illegal transfer of immigrants, officials said.

Provatas laid the charges after more than 100 immigrants were landed illegally south of Nafplion on December 30 and then arrested. They described their ordeal to police and alleged that nearly 300 people had drowned during their voyage.

Many of the immigrants told police that nearly 300 of their fellow travellers were forced on to another ship on December 25 in the Malta-Sicily channel. That ship sank after a collision with the vessel they were on, they said.
"The case has now been sent to an investigating magistrate and more people may be charged in the process," a court official in Nafplion told Reuters. No arrests have been made as yet.
